name: PosteAhora
tagline: Schedule and cross-post to Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, X, LinkedIn, Threads and more from one place, with analytics, an API and an MCP server

pricing.notes: Seat-based: one seat is one connected social account. Three tiers priced per seat per month: Basic 3.99, Essentials 6.99 (shown), Pro 12.99. Yearly billing is 30% off the monthly rate. priceMonthly is one Essentials seat; the site multiplies by the team size you type in.
pricing.freeTier: No free plan. You can connect up to two accounts to look around, but publishing needs a paid subscription, and every plan starts with a 3-day trial that takes a card.

tiers.name: Basic
tiers.limits: Per connected social account: 100 posts/month, 5 GB storage, 100 ideas, 1 API/MCP key; 1 workspace, no team
tiers.notes: The vendor prices per connected social account; billed $33.51/year at the displayed early-adopter rate.

tiers.name: Essentials
tiers.limits: Per connected social account: 200 posts/month, 10 GB storage, 300 ideas, 3 API/MCP keys; 10 workspaces, 5 team members
tiers.notes: The vendor prices per connected social account; billed $58.71/year at the displayed early-adopter rate.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: Per connected social account: unlimited posts and ideas, 25 GB storage, 5 API/MCP keys; unlimited workspaces/team
tiers.notes: The vendor prices per connected social account; billed $109.11/year at the displayed early-adopter rate.

pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual (page says save 30%); 3-day free trial
pricing.hiddenCosts: Every connected social profile is billed as a separate account, so the displayed price multiplies by the number of profiles. X links require Pro.

verdictSummary: The core loop, compose into a queue, tick a cron, publish, log the result, is one-shottable for the open networks like Bluesky, Mastodon and a Telegram channel. What you cannot one-shot is the reason PosteAhora exists: one-click posting to Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, Facebook, Threads and LinkedIn. Those APIs sit behind Meta App Review, TikTok's Content Posting API, YouTube quota and business verification, gates an individual often cannot even qualify for. On top of that sit per-platform media handling (Instagram carousels, TikTok photo vs video, small-Reel framing, X's 280-vs-25k length math), constant token-refresh babysitting as tokens expire and policies drift, and a hosted API plus MCP server so a coding agent can post for you. You can vibecode a personal cross-poster for the open networks in a sitting. You cannot vibecode the approvals.
coreLoopDIY: Compose posts into a slot-based queue, publish on schedule to open-API networks through per-network adapters, and log outcomes, with a push-to-post-by-hand fallback for the approval-gated platforms.
whatYouLose: one-click connect to approval-gated platforms (Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, Facebook, Threads, LinkedIn)
pre-approved platform OAuth apps you often cannot obtain as an individual
per-platform media handling and token-refresh babysitting as APIs and policies change
cross-network analytics, an ideas kanban, workspaces and team roles
the hosted API and MCP server that lets a coding agent post for you
moatNotes: platform-approved OAuth apps + endless per-network integration upkeep
whyPeopleStillPay: The hosted product ships with OAuth apps that Meta, TikTok, YouTube and LinkedIn have already put through business verification and app review, so connecting Instagram or TikTok is a click instead of the multi-week developer-app process you may not qualify for solo. It also absorbs constant API and policy churn, per-platform media quirks and token expiry, and exposes an API plus MCP server so your coding agent can schedule through it rather than you rebuilding and babysitting the poster yourself.

priorArt.name: Postiz
priorArt.desc: Open-source social scheduler, self-hostable, covers much of the DIY core for open-API networks.

priorArt.name: Mixpost
priorArt.desc: Self-hosted Laravel scheduler, a clean template for the compose/queue/publish loop.

alternatives.name: Postiz
alternatives.desc: The broadest open scheduler here; free means running PostgreSQL, Redis, Temporal and your own platform credentials.

facts.install: Hosted signup, or Docker Compose for self-hosting.
facts.engines: Optional AI/media features connect to OpenAI, ElevenLabs, fal.ai, Tavily, KieAI and Transloadit.
facts.dataFormat: PostgreSQL holds application data; Redis and Temporal support jobs; media is stored locally or in Cloudflare R2/S3-compatible storage.
facts.gapVsPaid: Postiz broadly matches the channels and developer interfaces but replaces PosteAhora's managed service with a multi-service deployment.
facts.setupBlocker: Hosted use is straightforward; self-hosting requires Docker, social OAuth apps, and a PostgreSQL, Redis and Temporal stack.

alternatives.name: BrightBean Studio
alternatives.desc: A startlingly complete free scheduler: approvals, inbox, analytics, clients, API and MCP, with someone else running the servers.

facts.install: Hosted signup, or clone the repository and deploy with Docker Compose or a supported PaaS.
facts.engines: No model is bundled; its REST API and MCP server connect external agents such as Claude Desktop/Code, Cursor or custom clients.
facts.dataFormat: Hosted data lives in BrightBean's cloud; self-hosted data uses PostgreSQL 16+ with media on local disk or S3-compatible storage.
facts.gapVsPaid: BrightBean does not document the same exact channel set and analytics depth as PosteAhora's purpose-built managed product.
facts.setupBlocker: Connecting social networks requires first-party platform developer/OAuth credentials; self-hosting also requires Docker or a PaaS.

alternatives.name: Mixpost Lite
alternatives.desc: A polished single-user scheduler with queues and basic analytics; the serious team features live in the paid edition.

facts.install: Docker Compose is recommended; a manual Laravel/Composer installation is also documented.
facts.dataFormat: MySQL stores application data, Redis handles queues/cache, and media uses local/public disk or S3-compatible storage.
facts.gapVsPaid: Mixpost Lite is single-user and lacks PosteAhora's API, MCP server and broader analytics workflow.
facts.setupBlocker: Requires a server with Docker plus social-platform app credentials; the manual path also needs PHP, Composer, Supervisor, cron, Redis and FFmpeg.

notes: Same shape as Post Bridge: the open-API core is a sitting, the big-platform set is the moat · approvals and integration upkeep, not code · plus an API and MCP server so your agent posts for you.
prompt:
Build me a personal social post scheduler to replace PosteAhora. Requirements:

- Node + Express + better-sqlite3; a localhost page with a compose box,
  image/video attach, and the queue ordered by send time.
- Targets with open APIs only: Bluesky (app password via @atproto/api),
  Mastodon (access token), and a Telegram channel (bot token). Creds in
  .env, one small adapter file per network so a fourth is addable later.
- For the approval-gated platforms people actually want (Instagram, TikTok,
  YouTube, Facebook, Threads, LinkedIn), do NOT fight their APIs: at post
  time send me an ntfy.sh push with the caption and media path so I post by
  hand in a minute. Say clearly in the README that these need approved
  developer apps and business verification you cannot one-shot.
- Slot-based queue: I define posting times per weekday in my timezone and
  new posts fill the next free slot; a post can also be pinned to an exact
  datetime or duplicated across networks with per-network text and counts.
- A node-cron tick every minute publishes due posts, marks each row sent or
  failed, retries failures 3 times with backoff, and marks before sending so
  nothing double-posts.
- Per-network character counter in the composer (X counts URLs as 23 and
  most emoji as 2); attached media stored in media/ next to the database,
  images resized per network with sharp.
- A history page of the last 100 sent posts linking to the live posts.
- Runs on my always-on box; localhost only, no accounts, no telemetry.
- Out of scope: cross-network analytics, teams and approvals, and
  per-platform video transcoding.
- README: getting a Bluesky app password, a Mastodon token and a Telegram
  bot token, plus an honest note that social APIs drift and this needs
  occasional patching.
